function: above_phy, p. 2: "A DNN model-based actor module produces the semantic extraction factors for UAVs", quantized into upload-or-drop decisions; transmit power comes from a classical bisection search (p. 9).
notes: Title and DOI 10.1109/JIOT.2024.3401229 on p. 1 match the work. UAV-assisted digital-twin synchronization in edge computing: UAVs upload semantic data to an edge server over OFDMA subchannels, and Lyapunov optimization gives per-slot resource allocation problems (p. 5-7). The learned DNN actor outputs only the semantic extraction factors (p. 7: "the DNN model outputs the extraction factors first"), quantized into binary synchronization indicators, upload or drop (p. 7), and is trained on samples "labeled by the critic module" with a cross-entropy loss (p. 9). The critic is classical: KKT for the edge CPU and the Gauss-Seidel method for UAV CPU and power (p. 8), with the power from "a bi-section search approach [39]" (p. 9). So the transmit power of the aerial link is not learned, and the exception for learned power or resource control in aerial links does not apply; the learning sets data compression and upload decisions, edge computing decisions above the physical layer. Not no_learning, since the DNN actor is the learned core of the method. The tiny-ML semantic encoders and decoders are only assumed pretrained (p. 10) and enter as workload models; had above_phy not applied, function would (semantic communication without any of the seven functions). Baselines MECS, UECS, MDTS; metrics latency, energy, drop ratio (p. 10-11).
